about: Measured by tools/measure_run.mjs; the ad draws this file and nothing else for its speed segment. Re-measure with a new release to replace it.

commands.per_document: start /affinity 40 litmus score --json --no-cache <one text file>, once per document, in turn (pass A)
commands.batch: start /affinity 40 litmus score --json --no-cache <a folder of all the documents>, one process (pass B)

basis.memory_basis: Windows process counters read by tools/sample_process.ps1 about every 50 ms for each litmus process: working set (physical memory held), peak working set, and private bytes (committed memory the process alone holds). The peaks are the largest of those readings and of the system-kept peak working set.
basis.cpu_basis: Processor seconds the litmus processes used (their TotalProcessorTime), divided by the wall seconds and by the machine's logical cores; the machine's own utilization is from os.cpus() times every 100 ms, so everything else is the machine minus litmus.
basis.engine: backends on this processor: scalar, avx2, avx2-sign (fastest avx2)

human.source: Project Gutenberg single short stories (subject "Short stories", English), ebooks 66143 to 79956 issued by 2026-11-08, from the mirror https://gutenberg.pglaf.org

ai.source: THU-KEG/LongStory sft_premise.jsonl (StoryWriter, arXiv 2506.16445), stories by GPT-4o-mini

trace.columns: t, litmus processor seconds in the interval, litmus working set MB, machine busy %, machine memory in use MB, then each core busy %
